chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rabi' ibn Abdullah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Poverty and fever do not come near the one habitual of the Hajj and the Umra'.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of frequent Hajj and Umra according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, establishes a dual benefit of consistent pilgrimage: spiritual resilience against material deprivation (*al-faqru*) and physical protection from illness (*al-humma*). In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as literal immunity but as a divine guarantee of sustenance and health for those who prioritize the House of God, reflecting the holistic view of worship in the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.
